'''Law and crime'''
* [[2022 Raleigh shootings]]
**Eighteen-year-old Austin Thompson, the perpetrator of a [[Mass shootings in the United States|mass shooting]] that killed five people in [[Raleigh, North Carolina|Raleigh]], [[North Carolina]], U.S., in 2022, is sentenced to [[Life imprisonment in the United States|life imprisonment]] without [[parole]] after pleading guilty to five counts of [[Murder in United States law|first-degree murder]] last month. [https://www.wral.com/news/ap/87693-judge-sentences-teen-to-life-without-parole-for-north-carolina-mass-shooting-that-killed-5/ (WRAL-TV)]
*[[2025–2026 Iranian protests]]
**[[Iran]] releases on [[bail]] three [[Iranian reformists|reformist]] [[Politics of Iran|political]] figures, including former [[Islamic Consultative Assembly|legislator]] [[Ebrahim Asgharzadeh]] and [[Union of Islamic Iran People Party]] secretary-general [[Azar Mansouri]], who were arrested during a recent crackdown on [[Political repression in the Islamic Republic of Iran|dissent]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/iran-releases-head-reform-front-coalition-isna-reports-2026-02-13/ (Reuters)]
*[[United Kingdom and the Gaza war]]
**The [[High Court of Justice]] rules that the [[Starmer ministry|British government]]'s decision to designate the [[Palestinian nationalism|pro-Palestinian]] activist group [[Palestine Action]] as a [[Terrorism in the United Kingdom|terrorist organization]] is [[English law|unlawful]] and disproportionate, while allowing the ban to remain in force pending appeal. The judgment prompts [[Law enforcement in the United Kingdom|police]] to suspend further arrests linked to support for the group. [https://edition.cnn.com/2026/02/13/uk/uk-palestine-action-ban-gbr-uk-intl (CNN)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2026 Bangladeshi general election]]
**The [[Bangladesh Nationalist Party]] wins a [[landslide victory]] in the parliamentary elections, winning 209 seats in the first election since the [[July Revolution (Bangladesh)|July Revolution]] that toppled former [[Prime Minister of Bangladesh|prime minister]] [[Sheikh Hasina]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/china/bangladesh-votes-landmark-election-after-gen-z-revolution-2026-02-11/ (Reuters)]
*[[2026 Liberal Party of Australia leadership spill]]
**[[Angus Taylor]] replaces [[Sussan Ley]] as [[Leader of the Opposition (Australia)|Leader of the Opposition]] following a leadership spill in the [[Liberal Party of Australia|Liberal Party]]. Ley subsequently resigns from politics, triggering a [[2026 Farrer by-election|by-election]] in her [[Division of Farrer|Farrer]] seat. [https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/live/2026/feb/13/australia-politics-live-liberals-leadership-spill-vote-angus-taylor-sussan-ley-libspill-anthony-albanese-indigenous-apology-anniversary-ntwnfb (''The Guardian'')]
*[[2027 Salvadoran legislative election]]
**[[Milagro Navas]], the mayor of La Libertad Este and [[El Salvador]]'s only opposition-aligned mayor, announces that she will run for re-election in 2027. [https://diario.elmundo.sv/ampArticle/milagro-navas-dice-esta-lista-para-buscar-reeleccion-en-la-libertad-este-en-2027?amp=1 (''El Mundo'')]
